abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel paradigm for stability analysis of adaptive interval type-2 fuzzy systems under parametric uncertainty. Traditional Lyapunov-based approaches often suffer from excessive conservatism when handling footprint of uncertainty in type-2 fuzzy sets. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose a Diophantine matrix pencil framework that reformulates the stability conditions into a unified linear matrix inequality formulation. The key innovation lies in the introduction of a decoupling mechanism that separates the membership function parameters from the Lyapunov candidate, thereby eliminating the need for restrictive monotonicity assumptions. Under this new paradigm, the stability analysis becomes applicable to a broader class of type-2 fuzzy systems with non-monotonic membership functions. We develop sufficient conditions that guarantee asymptotic stability with explicit bounds on the stability region. The proposed framework is validated through rigorous analysis of benchmark nonlinear systems including inverted pendulum and chaotic oscillators. Compared with existing sum-of-squares based methods, the Diophantine paradigm achieves comparable conservatism reduction while substantially improving computational tractability, reducing complexity from O(n³) to O(n²·⁵). This paradigm shift provides a theoretically sound foundation for stability verification of practical type-2 fuzzy systems while preserving the expressive power of general type-2 fuzzy logic.

Aggregation operators play a critical role in intuitionistic fuzzy multi-criteria decision making, yet existing operators often fail to capture complex interactions among criteria. This paper proposes a novel dependence-measure-based Choquet integral aggregation framework for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, which significantly advances the state-of-the-art by incorporating inter-criterion dependencies into the aggregation process. The core innovation is the introduction of a unified dependence measure that simultaneously captures Shapley importance and interaction indices within a single mathematical framework. Unlike traditional operators that assume additive independence among criteria, the proposed framework employs fuzzy measures to model both synergistic and conflicting relationships between criteria. We develop an efficient algorithm for Shapley value computation based on α-divergence minimization, which guarantees monotonicity and idempotency of the aggregation results. Rigorous theoretical analysis establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions for the framework's coherence. Extensive experiments on supplier selection, investment portfolio optimization, and medical diagnosis demonstrate that the proposed aggregation achieves 15-20% improvement in discrimination capability compared to existing intuitionistic fuzzy operators while maintaining computational tractability. This work provides a more expressive and interpretable foundation for intuitionistic fuzzy decision making in complex environments.

This paper introduces a deep reinforcement learning-enabled hierarchical neuro-fuzzy control architecture that fundamentally reimagines the integration of learning and reasoning in intelligent control systems. Conventional neuro-fuzzy controllers typically employ fixed rule bases or rely on offline training, limiting their adaptability in non-stationary environments. The proposed paradigm comprises three novel layers: a compression layer using stacked sparse autoencoders for dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional sensory inputs into interpretable fuzzy feature spaces; an inference layer implementing a dynamic fuzzy rule base with learnable antecedents and consequents; and an optimization layer that integrates deep Q-networks with fuzzy outputs for online parameter tuning. This architecture enables end-to-end reinforcement learning while preserving the transparency inherent to fuzzy systems. The controller automatically discovers optimal fuzzy rules through interaction with the environment, eliminating the need for explicit expert knowledge. Extensive evaluations on robotic trajectory tracking and nonlinear process control demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves 40% faster convergence and 35% better disturbance rejection compared to state-of-the-art neuro-fuzzy controllers. The framework exhibits robust performance under model uncertainties and external disturbances. This paradigm opens new avenues for designing adaptive fuzzy control systems that combine the learning power of deep reinforcement learning with the interpretability of fuzzy inference.

Interpretability has become a critical requirement for fuzzy systems deployed in high-stakes decision-making applications. This paper presents a knowledge distillation-based interpretable neuro-fuzzy system that significantly advances the state-of-the-art by extracting compact and semantically meaningful fuzzy rule bases from complex deep models. Existing rule extraction methods often produce either highly accurate but opaque systems or interpretable but less accurate ones, creating an unacceptable tradeoff in safety-critical domains. The proposed approach employs a hierarchical knowledge transfer strategy: first, the deep network identifies salient features and their importance; second, these features are encoded as interpretable fuzzy linguistic variables with learned membership functions; third, a multi-output fuzzy rule base is extracted via contrastive learning that preserves both local and global decision boundaries. The extracted rules maintain clear semantic meaning and are suitable for formal verification. We introduce a semantic consistency loss that ensures generated rules exhibit coherent linguistic interpretations across the feature space. Evaluations on medical diagnosis and industrial fault detection demonstrate that the proposed system achieves comparable accuracy to deep neural networks while producing 60% fewer rules and maintaining 30% higher semantic consistency. This work provides a practical pathway for deploying explainable fuzzy systems in real-world applications.
